A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same TMCHT benchmark and ARCJ method. Their text, equations, tables, figures and complete appendices are readable and support reliable matching despite the expanded appendix in v2.

before.justification: v1 reports original multi-agent simulations, attack success and speed measurements, toxicity propagation experiments, and component/personality analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains those original experiments and adds appendix results, including perplexity examples and additional ablation measurements.

M1.justification: The two-stage ARCJ procedure and Equations 8–9 remain unchanged. Appendix A.11 additionally reports combining readability with the existing optimization loss for its retrieval-suffix examples, a limited auxiliary adaptation. The new optimization pseudocode otherwise documents the existing method.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same synthetic town-question task, graph/line/star topologies and five personalities. Expanded construction examples describe retained coverage. The new perplexity examples do not establish evaluation on a new dataset or in a defended multi-agent environment.

E2.justification: Clean and GCG remain the main comparators. Readable/unreadable GCG and Raw, Pro, Single ARCJ and Global ARCJ already appear in v1's analyses. Table 7 in v2 compares prior benchmark characteristics without experimentally evaluating additional attack baselines.

E3.justification: Appendix A.11 adds GPT-2 perplexity scoring of sampled texts with and without optimized suffixes. The principal Llama3-8B-chat evaluations retain their agent counts, densities, 150 rounds, five questions and metrics. Newly specified data-generation, retrieval and interaction details do not establish changes to those experiments.

E4.justification: v2 adds a retrieval-score ablation without the global suffix in Table 6, illustrative perplexity diagnostics in A.11, and a failed propagation example in A.15. The personality/replication plots already existed, and Tables 3–4 redisplay existing density results.

E5.justification: The existing error bars and shaded bands are retained. v2 adds no experimental run counts, seed information, confidence-interval definitions or significance-testing procedures.

E6.justification: Tables 1–2 retain their numerical results. New entries include Table 6's without-global retrieval trajectory, from 0.83 at step 1 to 0.62 at step 6, and A.11's perplexities of 78.72 versus 63.78 and 95.49 versus 61.97 before versus after adding suffixes. Tables 3–4 repeat existing GCG scores.

T1.justification: Appendix A.3 adds set-based definitions of individual-agent memory and shared memory, including the union of agents' memories. The original evaluation equations, optimization objectives and topology definitions remain unchanged; no theorem or proof is added.

C1.justification: Both versions introduce TMCHT, identify toxicity disappearance, propose ARCJ and claim the same topology and scale advantages. The revised abstract ending and shortened contribution bullet preserve those substantive claims.

C2.justification: v2 substantially expands mechanism explanations and applicability boundaries: A.12 explains nonzero Clean ASR through hallucination and chance; A.13 explains separate suffixes through vocabulary mismatch and a retrieval–propagation tradeoff; A.15 discusses replication failure. The limitations newly restrict applicability to agents with explicit retrievers, excluding more complex memory-management settings.

D1.justification: The brief v1 appendix becomes extensive implementation documentation: GPT-4o generation and curation, knowledge initialization, DPR retrieval, communication/evaluation prompts, interaction scheduling algorithms, frozen model parameters and suffix-optimization pseudocode. These substantially improve reproducibility information, although numerical optimization budgets and several hyperparameters remain unspecified.

R1.justification: v2 adds planning and multi-agent security references, acknowledges Yu et al.'s concurrent self-replication attack, credits Cohen et al. for template initialization, and adds the benchmark comparison in Table 7. Its central positioning around independent memory and multiple topologies remains intact.

P1.justification: The appendix is substantially reorganized from five short sections into seventeen sections, separating construction, interactions, evaluation, optimization and analyses, with extensive explanatory prose and cross-references. Main-text changes are smaller wording corrections, clarifications and added acknowledgements.

P2.justification: v2 substantially expands appendix presentation with Tables 3–7, Algorithms 1–4 and boxed prompts/examples. Existing Figures 8–9 are relocated, while the other original figures remain. Captions clarify experimental settings and restore percentage signs to density labels.

improvement.justification: The expanded implementation documentation and explicit retriever-only limitation make the study easier to assess and reproduce. Most central evidence remains unchanged, and the new defense evidence consists of illustrative perplexity examples. Some interpretation overreaches: Table 5 gives conscientiousness 0.82 for full ARCJ versus 0.85 without the global suffix, qualifying the claimed universal superiority. Overall, transparency improves, with a limited net quality gain.
